anti_overlap: fd-bevy-input-state-revisit covers which mouse event primitive triggers the right-click — this agent covers what happens after the click is received: coordinate math, content assembly, and lifecycle
fd-selection-polymorphism-revisit covers how left-click selection updates the Selection enum — this agent covers right-click tooltip, which is independent of Selection state
fd-overlay-state-machine covers tooltip dismiss via Esc/backtick at the OverlayState level — this agent covers tooltip content correctness and edge-clamp, not dismiss routing
decision_lens: For the sticky right-click tooltip: (1) is the tile-to-world coordinate mapping correct for non-square atlas cells, (2) is content refresh per-tick derived from a fresh snapshot query rather than a captured entity list, (3) is edge-clamp implemented to prevent the tooltip from overflowing the window at bottom-right tiles, (4) is the lifecycle managed via Display::None or despawn and what are the ECS implications of each choice?
focus: Sticky tooltip correctness — all-entities priority-order content assembly, per-tick content refresh when entities move off-tile, edge-clamp positioning in Bevy 0.18 UI, despawn vs Display::None lifecycle, and viewport_to_world_2d coordinate math for right-click tile identification.
name: fd-tooltip-content-lifecycle
persona: Apply the perspective of a game UI programmer who has implemented context-sensitive tooltips in ECS-based games — they care about whether tooltip content is always derived from the current snapshot (never from a cached entity list that goes stale), measure correctness by whether entities that leave a tile drop out of the tooltip within one tick, and flag any design where the tooltip's position is computed in screen space without accounting for atlas cell aspect ratio (23×36px cells where world→tile Y must use cell_size.y not cell_size.x).
review_areas: viewport_to_world_2d Result handling: Bevy 0.18 camera.viewport_to_world_2d returns Result<Vec2, ViewportConversionError>, not Option — right-click picking must handle Err (e.g. right-click outside viewport) without panicking; also confirm the spec accounts for the Y-axis inversion noted in open question 3 (tile (0,0) at world origin, Bevy Y-up means tile row 79 renders above center)

Cell aspect ratio in tile identification: open question 4 notes that tile_size = atlas.cell_size.x but cells are 23×36 — if world→tile conversion for right-click uses tile_size for both X and Y, the Y tile index will be wrong by a factor of 36/23; the spec for picking.rs must use cell_size.y for the Y division

Content assembly priority order: the locked decision specifies Elf > Building > Flora > Terrain — the tooltip system must query the snapshot for all entities at the identified tile and render them in that order; verify the spec describes how 'all entities at tile (x,y)' is assembled (likely: filter snapshot.elves, buildings, flora by pos == tile_pos) and that Terrain is always appended last as a fallback

Per-tick content refresh: locked decision 4 states tooltip content refreshes from the current snapshot each tick, with entities that moved off-tile dropping out — verify the spec describes a TooltipState resource that stores the pinned tile position (not entity ids) so that each frame the tooltip system re-queries the snapshot at that tile position; storing entity ids would cause stale content if the entity moves

All-entities-gone dismiss: if all entities leave the pinned tile (e.g. elf walks away, building demolished, flora harvested), the tooltip should auto-dismiss — verify this case is described in the spec; the condition is: snapshot re-query at tile_pos returns zero entities (only Terrain remains, which is always present — so the condition is actually zero non-Terrain entities if Terrain is excluded from the 'all gone' check)

Edge-clamp and GlobalZIndex: the tooltip must not overflow the window at bottom-right corners — the spec notes ~200px width matching sidebar; verify the spec describes clamping tooltip top/left to window bounds using Val::Px with a computed clamp, and that Tooltip is assigned GlobalZIndex(300) per the proposed ladder, placing it above HUD(0), Sidebar(0), Screen(100), PauseMenu(200)

severity_examples.condition: Always reproducible on any non-square atlas; manifests immediately on first right-click
severity_examples.scenario: world→tile conversion uses cell_size.x (23) for both X and Y divisions — right-clicking on tile row 20 identifies it as tile row 32 (20 * 36/23 ≈ 31.3), so the tooltip shows entities from the wrong tile; this is invisible at compile time and causes persistent incorrect tooltip content

severity_examples.condition: Always reproducible; entity movement happens every tick in active colonies
severity_examples.scenario: TooltipState stores a Vec of entity_ids captured at right-click time — when the elf moves off the tile the next tick, the tooltip still shows 'Mira — weaving' because it displays from the captured list rather than re-querying the snapshot at the pinned tile position

severity_examples.condition: Reproducible on any tile within ~200px of the bottom or right window edge
severity_examples.scenario: Tooltip spawned as a Bevy UI node at right-click world position without edge-clamping — at the bottom-right corner of the map, the tooltip overflows the window boundary and partial text is clipped, making it impossible to read building/terrain lines

success_hints: Verify the spec's picking.rs pseudo-code uses camera.viewport_to_world_2d(cursor_pos)? and divides world_pos.x by cell_size.x and world_pos.y by cell_size.y separately — not a single tile_size for both
Check TooltipState stores tile_pos: IVec2 (the pinned tile coordinate), not a Vec<EntityId>, so the update system re-queries snapshot each frame
Confirm the spec lists GlobalZIndex(300) for the tooltip node and describes clamping logic that keeps the tooltip within the window bounds
task_context: Reviewing the tooltip design in the Revel-14e locked-decisions document (decisions 3 and 4, plus open questions 3 and 4) alongside the er-renderer atlas and tiles source to verify the sticky tooltip's coordinate math, content lifecycle, edge-clamping, and dismiss logic are correctly specified before implementation begins.
